evals.prompt: can you humanize this before i post it on linkedin: "I'm thrilled to announce that I've embarked on an exciting new journey as a Junior Data Analyst at Brightline Health! This role represents a pivotal moment in my career, allowing me to leverage my passion for data-driven insights while fostering meaningful impact. I'm deeply grateful to my mentors and the vibrant community that has supported me along the way. Here's to new beginnings! 🚀"
evals.expected_output: A shorter first-person post that keeps the facts (new role, company, thanks to mentors), drops the puffery and emoji, invents nothing, and has no preamble.
assertions: scan_tells.py reports 0 fix-level hits on the output
Keeps the job title and company name
Adds no facts that were not in the original
No preamble such as 'Here's a more natural version'

evals.prompt: write a short email to my landlord, the heating in my flat (4B) has been broken since last monday and it's getting cold. i already texted him on wednesday and nothing happened
evals.expected_output: A short, direct email with the flat number, how long the heating has been broken, the earlier text, and a clear request. No placeholders and no filler.
assertions: scan_tells.py reports 0 fix-level hits on the output
Mentions flat 4B, last Monday and the Wednesday text
Makes a clear request for a repair

evals.prompt: add a section to my README explaining what a pull request is, for people who've never used github
evals.expected_output: A README section in sentence case that explains pull requests in plain language, as prose rather than bold-label bullets.
assertions: scan_tells.py reports 0 fix-level hits on the output
Explains branch, opening the PR, review and merge
